cultural.vision_reason: The picture shows a child’s handwoven and heavily embroidered tunic with geometric patterns and tassels, a garment plausibly made and worn by Hausa people of Niger.

physical.title: tunic
physical.summary: Child's bolero composed of hand plain woven cotton: dyed red blue and bleached white warps and dyed black blue and bleached white wefts. This combination of warps and wefts this creates red warp stripes at regular intervals crossed by pairs of black weft stripes at regular intervals on a light blue background. The front of the bolero is heavily embroidered with geometric patterns in dyed red, green, black, red and blue wool. There are also a number of tassels in dyed red and green wool attached. The back of bolero has a single panel of dyed red wool supplementary weft work. There are also sixteen areas of tassels created using supplementary weft work in dyed red and blue cotton. The sleeves and base of the garment are edges with dyed orange synthetic material.
